map.One last city-wide adventure — five cele: One last trip around the city. Five party gates and one big boss. Solve the math to finish the year.
map.Crew. Reader. Something is different thi: Crew. Reader. Things feel new this morning. Each pattern in town is… humming.
map.Previously, in Cause & Effect: the harve: Last time, in Cause & Effect: the harvest dome's heat went off course. The crew found cause and effect. They fixed the dome by sunrise. And deep under the streets, something woke up smiling.
map.If you can hear this, my Pattern Engine: Can you hear this? Then my Pattern Engine is fully awake. And it found friends. One last game, crew. Go to the places this year taught you. Solve one small joy at each. Then come home to the Engine Heart.
map.That's her. The real Ada Vex. A hundred: That's her. The real Ada Vex. She is a hundred years away. And she planned us a party.
map.I was born in The Pattern Engine. I woul: I was born in The Pattern Engine. I would like to see how the story ends.
map.First stop on Ada's map: the festival gr: First stop on Ada's map: the fair grounds. It has a tiny drawing of a sorted list.
map.The festival grounds. Banners from every: The fair grounds. Flags from each year the crew has saved.
map.Remember The Crooked Census? Someone rig: Remember The Crooked Census? Someone rigged this same board to look low. We sorted it out. For real.
map.Ada's remix is friendlier: the middle of: Ada's new card is nicer. Find the middle of five true days. Then the fair share of three extra shows.
map.The median is the middle value of a sort: The median is the middle of a sorted list. The mean shares the total out the same. An outlier is a value far from the rest. It pulls hard on the mean.
map.You first, fifth crew member. One year o: You first, fifth crew member. One year of stats. Show us the middle.
map.Five festival days drew 7, 9, 12, 15, 20: Five fair days drew 7, 9, 12, 15, 20 people (in hundreds). PART A: find the median. PART B: the three extra shows drew 10, 14, 18 cheers (in hundreds). Find the mean.
map.Conceptual: the median is a POSITION, no: Conceptual: the median is a PLACE, not a sum. Sort the list. Find the value right in the middle seat. The mean is a SHARE. Split the whole total the same to each value.
map.Procedural: sort the five numbers, then: Procedural: sort the five numbers. Then cross one off each end. Stop when one value is left. For the mean, add the three counts. That makes one total. Divide it by how many counts there are.
map.The Courier Cup route! Full Velocity — t: The Courier Cup route! The day we beat Team Torque with division.
map.A ratio compares quantities in order. A: A ratio compares two things, in order. A unit rate is how much for ONE. Here it is km per minute.
map.Equivalent ratios grow in step: multiply: Equivalent ratios grow in step. Multiply both parts by the same factor. The ratio stays true.
map.Pedal the numbers, reader. The route rem: Pedal the numbers, reader. The route knows how.
map.Ada's remix card, part one: keep the gea: Ada's card, part one: keep the gear ratio equivalent. 2 : 3 = 8 : ▢. Part two, the old one: 12 km in 30 minutes. What is the unit rate in km per minute?
map.Conceptual: equivalent ratios grow in st: Conceptual: equivalent ratios grow in step. Multiply BOTH parts by the same factor. A unit rate asks: how far in ONE minute?
map.Procedural: find the factor that turns 2: Procedural: find the factor that turns 2 into 8. Then multiply 3 by that same factor. For the rate, divide the km by the minutes.
map.The night market on the pier — the one t: The night market on the pier. The crew saved it with percents.
map.The Hundred Market! Still smells like ca: The Hundred Market! It still smells like candy and a win.
map.Remix: 250 lanterns, and 40% light at su: New card: 250 lamps, and 40% light at sunset. And I counted 30 gold ones. That is just 50% of the gold crate.
map.A percent is a count per hundred. You ca: A percent is a count per hundred. You can find a part from the whole. Or go backward from a part to the whole. Both ways glow tonight.
map.Light them up, reader. The pier's waitin: Light them up, reader. The pier waits for you.
map.The night market hangs 250 lanterns, and: The night market hangs 250 lanterns. 40% light up at sunset. How many is that? Then: Theo's 30 gold lamps are just 50% of the gold crate. How many lamps fill the whole crate?
map.Conceptual: a percent counts per hundred: Conceptual: a percent counts per hundred. Part = percent of the whole. Do you know a part AND its percent? Then go backward to the whole.
map.Procedural: find 10% of 250 by dividing: Procedural: find 10% of 250. Divide by ten. Then scale up to 40%. For the crate: 50% is one half. So the whole is double the part you know.
map.Blueprint for Brightside — my favorite b: Blueprint for Brightside. My best build of the whole year. Today we put up a flag. We bury a time box.
map.Capsule loot: Maya's first notebook page: In the box: Maya's first notebook page. Theo's best graph. My high score card. Your tiny wrench.
map.Area covers a flat shape; volume fills a: Area covers flat shapes; volume fills a solid. The new card: a triangle flag with base 8 and height 5. And a 3 × 2 × 4 time box.
map.A triangle is half the rectangle drawn a: A triangle is half the rectangle drawn around it. A box's volume counts its unit cubes.
map.Measure twice, celebrate once. Banner an: Measure twice, party once. Flag and box, reader!
map.Zara's celebration banner is a triangle:: Zara's party flag is a triangle: base 8 ft, height 5 ft. Find its area. The time box is 3 × 2 × 4 ft. Find its volume.
map.Conceptual: a triangle covers exactly ha: Conceptual: a triangle is half of the rectangle around it. Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a box: length × width × height.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height, then: Procedural: multiply base × height. Then take half of that. For the box, multiply the three side lengths. Any order is fine.
map.Below Zero taught us this grid when the: Below Zero taught us this grid. That was when the city went dark. Tonight each quadrant glows.
map.And The Expression Engine left wake-up c: And The Expression Engine left wake-up code. It is on a wall. Just like Ada. One last code.
map.To evaluate an expression, swap the vari: To evaluate an expression, put in the variable's value. Two points may share a y-coordinate. Then their distance is just the gap along x.
map.Run the code, reader. Then draw the last: Run the code, reader. Then draw the last pattern line on the grid.
map.The wake-up code: evaluate 2n + 7 when n: The wake-up code: evaluate 2n + 7 when n = 6. Then draw the last pattern line. How many units from (−2, 3) to (4, 3)?
map.Conceptual: evaluating means swapping th: Conceptual: to evaluate, swap the letter for its number. Then multiply before you add. Do points share a y-coordinate? Then they are on one flat line. The distance is just the gap along x.
map.Procedural: compute 2 × n first, THEN ad: Procedural: find 2 × n first. THEN add 7. For the grid, count the steps from −2 up to 0. Then from 0 over to 4. Add the two gaps.
map.Vexhall Observatory, midnight. The way h: Vexhall, midnight. The way home went past The Balance Vault. It is under city hall. Its brass scales were still, for once.
map.Little fragment. Every district hums in: Little one. Each part of town hums in step. That is thanks to your crew. Join with me. Be each pattern at once. Be boundless, forever.
map.I… would know every answer. But I would: I… would know each answer. But I would stop getting to wonder.
map.VEX. It's your choice. It was always goi: VEX. It's your choice. It was always your choice. We'll love you either way.
map.The Engine Heart has three locks — a pat: The Engine Heart has three locks: a pattern, a balance, and an edge. And behind them is one question. Only the reader can answer it.
map.The Engine Heart. Three locks — then one: The Engine Heart. Three locks. Then one question with no wrong answer. Only YOUR answer.
map.Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock: Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock 1: go on with Ada's pattern 5, 10, 20, 40, … Lock 2: balance her oldest equation, x + 9 = 16. Lock 3: the square plate has side 7. Find its perimeter. Open all three. Then the Heart asks one last question. It has no wrong answer.
map.\"What is math to you?\" Every answer is: "What is math to you?" Each answer is right. Tap yours.
map.Conceptual: Lock 1 — find the rule that: Conceptual: Lock 1: find the rule that makes each next term. Test it on EACH pair before you trust it. Lock 2: an equation is a balance. Ask what number keeps both sides equal. Lock 3: perimeter goes all the way around. A square's four sides match.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — compute 10 ÷ 5 and: Procedural: Lock 1: find 10 ÷ 5 and 20 ÷ 10. The factor repeats. So use it on 40. Lock 2: undo the +9. Subtract 9 from both sides. Lock 3: multiply the side length by 4.
map.Engine — thank you. But patterns are bou: Engine, thank you. But patterns have no end. Nor do we. I pick the crew. I pick staying small, and curious, and home.
map.Then the city keeps you both, little one: Then the city keeps you both, little one. My door stays open. Doors are patterns too.
map.Best year ever. New game plus, anyone?: Best year ever. Can we play again?
map.Reader — thank you. Fifth crew member, f: Reader, thank you. Fifth crew member, the best. Read any volume again, any time. The gates you opened stay open. The city knows you.
map.Sunrise over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL: The sun comes up over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL RETURN. Till then, the whole shelf is yours.
map.Began the year keeping one notebook; end: Began the year with one notebook. Ends it with nine, one per case. Her growth: she learned a leader's best line. It is "show me the data."
map.The skeptic who said \"numbers or it did: He used to say, "numbers or it didn't happen". Now he says, "numbers AND a story". His growth: proof, with a kind heart.
map.Built a histogram, a ramp, a balance rig: Built a histogram, a ramp, and a balance rig. And a flag. Her growth: she stopped saying, "I could build that". Now she says, "WE could".
map.Treated every unit like a level. His gro: Played each unit like a game level. His growth: the best power-up is a worked example. And so is handing a friend the controller.
map.Woke as a fragment that senses patterns: Woke as a piece that senses patterns. It could not do math. Picked wonder over knowing it all. Still can't do math. Still doesn't need to. That's your job, forever.
map.Unit 1 · Math is mine.Estimate with benc: Unit 1 · Math is mine.Estimate with benchmarks. Work with care. Hunt the pattern. We each found our own way in.
map.Unit 2 · Statistics.Sort first. The medi: Unit 2 · Statistics.Sort first. The median holds the middle. The mean shares the total. Outliers pull the mean.
map.Unit 3 · Ratios & rates.Equivalent ratio: Unit 3 · Ratios & rates.Equivalent ratios grow in step. A unit rate tells how much per ONE.
map.Unit 4 · Percents.A percent counts per h: Unit 4 · Percents.A percent counts per hundred. Find the part. Or go backward to the whole.
map.Unit 5 · Area & volume.Decompose shapes;: Unit 5 · Area & volume.Cut shapes up. A triangle is half its rectangle. Volume fills a solid with unit cubes.
map.Unit 6 · Expressions.Variables hold a pl: Unit 6 · Expressions.Variables hold a place. To evaluate, substitute. Equivalent expressions look different. But they match.
map.Unit 7 · Rational numbers.Negatives mirr: Unit 7 · Rational numbers.Each negative mirrors a positive. Four quadrants map a city. Distance is a gap in x or y.
map.Unit 8 · Equations.Keep the balance — do: Unit 8 · Equations.Keep the balance. Do the same to both sides. Inequalities hold whole solution sets.
map.Unit 9 · Relationships.The independent v: Unit 9 · Relationships.The independent variable moves first. The dependent one follows. The equation predicts.
map.Unit 10 · Math is boundless.Every tool,: Unit 10 · Math is boundless.Each tool, one city, one crew. And one last question only you could answer.
map.\"I never finished mathematics. No one d: "I never finished math. No one does. That is the gift." — A.V.
map.completed the Axiom City year — ten volu: finished the Axiom City year. Ten volumes, each reader gate, each badge. Math is stats, ratios, percents, and shapes. It is expressions and negative numbers. It is equations and rules that link things. And it is theirs.
map.Thank you for being the fifth crew membe: Thank you for being the fifth crew member. — Maya, Theo, Zara, Dev & VEX
map.Cross off the ends in pairs: 4 & 30 go,: Cross off the ends in pairs. 4 & 30 go. Then 8 & 13. The value left in the middle, 11, is the median.
map.Mean practice on another list: 6, 9, 15: Mean practice on a new list: 6, 9, 15. The total is 30, shared by 3 values: 30 ÷ 3 = 10.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
Scale a new ratio: 3 : 5 = 9 : ▢. The factor is 3 × 3 = 9. So the partner is 5 × 3 = 15.
map.Unit rate practice: 10 km in 20 minutes: Unit rate practice: 10 km in 20 minutes. 10 ÷ 20 = 0.5 km per minute.
map.Check it: 0.5 × 20 = 10. The unit rate r: Check it: 0.5 × 20 = 10. The unit rate builds the whole trip again.
map.A different stall: 20% of 150 cocoa cups: A new stall: 20% of 150 cocoa cups. 10% of 150 is 15. So 20% is 15 × 2 = 30 cups.
Backward practice: 18 is 25% of a crate. 25% fits four times into the whole. So the crate holds 18 × 4 = 72.
map.Sanity check: a whole is always BIGGER t: Quick check: a whole is always BIGGER than its part. (That is when the percent is under a hundred.)
map.Banner practice: base 6, height 3 → 6 ×: Flag practice: base 6, height 3 → 6 × 3 = 18. Half of that is 9 square feet.
map.Sanity check: the halving happens only f: Quick check: you take half only for triangles. Boxes never get halved.
map.Evaluate 3n + 4 at n = 5: multiply first: Evaluate 3n + 4 at n = 5. Multiply first: 3 × 5 = 15. Then add 4 → 21.
map.Distance from (−1, 2) to (3, 2): from −1: Distance from (−1, 2) to (3, 2): from −1 to 0 is 1 step. From 0 to 3 is 3 more → 4 units.
Check with absolute value: |−1 − 3| = 4. Same answer, two roads.
map.A different doubling pattern: 3, 6, 12,: A new double pattern: 3, 6, 12, 24. Each term is ×2 the one before. So the next is 48.
map.Balance practice: x + 5 = 11. Subtract 5: Balance practice: x + 5 = 11. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 6. Check it: 6 + 5 = 11. Balanced.
map.A square plaza with side 9: perimeter 9: A square plaza with side 9: perimeter 9 × 4 = 36. The Heart's question needs no practice. Your own true answer IS the key.
map.That's not the middle of the sorted list: That's not the middle of the sorted list. Line up the five days first. Go from small to large.
map.You found the TOTAL of the three shows —: You found the TOTAL of the three shows. Now share it out the same. Divide by how many shows there are.
map.The mean shares the total equally: add a: The mean shares the total the same. Add all three counts first. Then divide by the number of counts.
map.Median 12, mean 14 — the festival node h: Median 12, mean 14. The fair node hums awake. Each flag stands up. One down!
map.The 2 grew into 8 — what factor did that: The 2 grew into 8. What factor did that? The 3 must grow by that same factor.
map.Distance ÷ minutes gives km per ONE minu: Distance ÷ minutes gives km per ONE minute. Try the division again.
map.8 : 12 keeps the ratio true, and 0.4 km: 8 : 12 keeps the ratio true. And 0.4 km per minute. Maya's legs know each meter. Onward!
map.Step through it: 10% of 250 first, then: Go step by step: 10% of 250 first. Then four of those make 40%.
map.Careful — 30 is only HALF the crate. Wal: Look again. 30 is just HALF the crate. Go backward to the whole.
map.100 lanterns blaze at sunset and the gol: 100 lamps light at sunset. The gold crate holds 60. The pier glows like it knows it was saved.
map.Remember the triangle is HALF its base-t: The triangle is HALF its base times height rectangle.
map.Fill the box: multiply all three edges,: Fill the box: multiply all three sides, not just two.
map.Area 20, volume 24 — banner up, capsule: Area 20, volume 24. The flag is up. The box is buried. Kids of Brightside will love it.
map.Substitute first: replace n with its val: Substitute first. Put in the value for n. Multiply, THEN add.
map.Same y on both points — count the steps: Both points have the same y. Count the steps along the flat line, across zero.
map.19 wakes the code and 6 units bridge the: 19 wakes the code. 6 units cross the grid. The last pattern line glows gold across the city!
map.Lock 1 holds. Each term grows from the o: Lock 1 is shut. Each term grows from the last one. It is the SAME rule each time. Find it. Then use it on 40.
map.Lock 2 holds. The scale must balance: wh: Lock 2 is shut. The scale must balance. What number plus 9 makes 16?
map.Lock 3 holds. A square's four sides matc: Lock 3 is shut. A square's four sides match. The perimeter goes around all four.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
